import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Filter for the latest year in the dataset to get a current snapshot
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest_year = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year].copy()

# Identify the top N most common dog breeds
N = 10
top_breeds = df_latest_year['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(N).index.tolist()

# Filter the DataFrame to include only the rows corresponding to these top N breeds
df_filtered_breeds = df_latest_year[df_latest_year['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_breeds)]

# Create a cross-tabulation (contingency table) to count the occurrences of each
# top breed within each Zurich district ('KreisLang').
# This table will be used for the heatmap, with districts as rows and breeds as columns.
breed_district_counts = pd.crosstab(df_filtered_breeds['KreisLang'], df_filtered_breeds['Rasse1Text'])

# Ensure that all top breeds are present as columns in the cross-tabulation,
# and that their order matches the 'top_breeds' list (from most to least popular).
# Fill any potential missing breed-district combinations with 0.
breed_district_counts = breed_district_counts.reindex(columns=top_breeds, fill_value=0)

# Sort the districts on the y-axis (rows) by their numerical 'KreisCd' for logical order.
# First, get unique district names and their corresponding codes from the original data.
district_order_df = df_latest_year[['KreisCd', 'KreisLang']].drop_duplicates().sort_values('KreisCd')
# Then, filter this ordered list to only include districts present in our current cross-tabulation.
district_order_filtered_names = [d for d in district_order_df['KreisLang'].tolist() if d in breed_district_counts.index]
# Reindex the cross-tabulation rows according to this sorted district list.
breed_district_counts = breed_district_counts.reindex(district_order_filtered_names)

# Create the heatmap visualization
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8)) # Set a larger figure size for better readability of labels and annotations
sns.heatmap(
    breed_district_counts,
    annot=True,          # Display the count values on the heatmap cells
    fmt='d',             # Format the annotations as integers
    cmap='viridis',      # Choose a perceptually uniform colormap
    linewidths=.5,       # Add lines to separate cells for clarity
    linecolor='lightgray' # Set the color of the separating lines
)

# Add a descriptive title and axis labels
plt.title(f'Distribution of Top {N} Dog Breeds Across Zurich Districts ({latest_year})', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Dog Breed', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Zurich District', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability, especially with longer breed names
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
# Keep y-axis labels horizontal
plt.yticks(rotation=0)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping and ensure everything fits
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
